audit.why: Emerald+ 58.8% over 267 games. The packet flags the chart as contradicting it, but the chart is a lane chart and the win rate is a game win rate: Azir owns the lane end to end and Aurelion Sol still wins games off the scaling curve. Rows 0-3 and row 6 left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two chart rows disagreed across the layers. Full phases[4].side and phases[5].side said 'Skill'; content win[4] and win[5] both said 'Azir'. Row 6 already agreed ('Skill' on both).
audit.why: The packet levelChart gives Azir six stages and 'Skill' only at 2+ items. Level 6 is his because Emperor's Divide is a knockback wall that shoves you off a channel and out of your own black hole; First item is his because Arise! is a 1.5s cooldown, so there is no window where a soldier is not standing between you and the wave.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side and phases[5].side move to 'Azir', and both whys are rewritten in the same proposal to argue for Azir rather than describing the owner's spikes. Ratings left at 6/10 to match row 3, which is already Azir at 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and content late describe a 'Comet threat' and a 'global Comet'.
audit.why: Pre-rework Aurelion Sol language. The live kit has Breath of Light and The Skies Descend; the ultimate is 1250 range, not global.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten around the stacked beam and The Skies Descend.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single actionable weakness in Azir's kit was never stated: Shifting Sands can only dash to a Sand Soldier.
audit.why: Riot's E text: 'shields himself briefly and dashes to one of his Sand Soldiers'. With no soldier placed, his 22s escape does not exist — and the same text says the dash HALTS on the first enemy champion it hits, so it does not carry him through you. The page instead gave 'engage the window after he burns it', which waits for a cooldown that a soldier placement can make irrelevant.
audit.corrected: Stated in dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, report[5].t, tradeGood and ahead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Emperor's Divide's knockback was never connected to Aurelion Sol's kit at all.
audit.why: Riot's R text: a wall of soldiers that charges forward 'knocking back and damaging enemies'. Both of Aurelion Sol's core abilities are interruptible channels and his black hole is a zone he needs the enemy to stand in, so a knockback removes the channel AND removes the target from the singularity in one cast. It is also only 250 range, so he has to be close to use it — which is precisely what flying at him gives him.
audit.corrected: Stated in tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d, report[5].t and content mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: content early said his shield 'can straight-up block your star's damage', and wants.foe[0] said he can 'shield-block your Q star's damage'.
audit.why: Shifting Sands grants a brief shield — it absorbs damage, it does not block or nullify an ability. Against a multi-second beam channel that distinction matters: the shield eats the opening ticks and the rest still lands.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to say the shield absorbs the front of the channel.

audit.why: Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1 — identical to Astral Flight, so his escape and yours refresh together. Arise! is 1.5s and gated by mana (40 at rank 1), Conquering Sands 14s at rank 1, Emperor's Divide 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the Shifting Sands, Astral Flight and Emperor's Divide numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] hedged: 'his shield and zoning still generally win exchanges'.
audit.why: 'Generally' says nothing. The behaviour is that they win exchanges.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed: dosFull[1].d ('Farm the back line with E executes') was the tradeGood string and dontsFull[2].d ('Fly W into his cooldown-loaded face') was the tradeBad string.
audit.why: Both bodies now explain their own titles.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d rewritten around the black hole's 12s and 90 mana; dontsFull[2].d around Emperor's Divide's 250 range and knockback.

notes: suspectNames flagged 'Use Emperor's Divide' in wants.foe[2] as a probable wrong name — FALSE POSITIVE. Emperor's Divide is Azir's real R per the kit file; I left wants.foe[2] alone. Chart: rows 4 and 5 (Level 6, First item) said 'Skill' in the full layer and 'Azir' in the content layer; I moved the sides to Azir to match the packet and content, and rewrote both whys in the same proposal so each sentence now argues for Azir. Row 6 already agreed on 'Skill' and was untouched. Two things I deliberately did NOT write, because the kit cannot support them: (1) any range comparison between Conquering Sands (740) and Breath of Light (750). The kit gives no Sand Soldier attack range, and his effective reach is soldier position plus soldier range, not 740 — quoting 740 against 750 would read as 'you out-range him', which is false. (2) Any claim about whether Falling Star's stun or the black hole's pull can catch Azir mid-Shifting-Sands; Riot's text says the dash halts on a champion hit but says nothing about being interrupted. Also unverified: whether Emperor's Divide's knockback specifically pulls a target out of the black hole's pull field (I wrote that the knockback removes you from your own zone, which follows from it being a displacement and the zone requiring the enemy to stand in it, but I have no tested source); tenacity/QSS on Falling Star. The pre-rework 'Comet' / 'Q star' language shows up here too, in spikes[0], spikes[3], early, late, wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0] — six of six matchups in my slice, so this is a champion-wide content problem rather than a per-matchup one.
